findings.reason: a guard whose control is absent cannot be shown to fire, and here the section either adds a second control or splits into two nodes, both of which change what is built and gated.
findings.text: §33's deliverable is two independently-failing guards (the `deferred_outcome` liveness read in `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py` and the review-queued window in `reckon/crew/obligations.py`) but its single declared negative control — "with `deferred_outcome` testing `alive is True` again, the first case reads `scoring`" — exercises only the first; nothing makes the second guard fire, so a review-queued window that never closes or closes immediately passes green

findings.reason: the mechanism as written cannot compute the window it asserts; the plan must name the figure's source (the constant, or a value plumbed onto the run) or the node invents a constant the plan disclaims.
findings.text: part 2 fixes the duty window to "one reflex sweep" and asserts "the sweep interval is the reflex's own, not a new figure", but that interval is the follower's `--sweep-interval`, defaulting to `DEFAULT_SWEEP_SECONDS` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1654-1656), and it is recorded on no pointer, registration or status row the duty scan reads — so the obligations deriver, running on the producer host, has no value to measure "less than one reflex sweep old" against, while a non-default cadence makes the named figure wrong for that session

findings.reason: the implementer reaches the verdict through the named module and symbol, so a mistaken section pointer does not change what is built; it is a citation error only.
findings.text: "the stream-aware verdict seat §10 gave `process_gone`" points at §10 of this plan, "A run nobody will come back to is reported, never capped", which concerns forgotten-run reporting and says nothing of `process_gone` or a stream-aware liveness verdict; the stream-aware verdict described here landed from a different plan (`a-seat-held-elsewhere-is-not-restarted`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the module and symbol citations resolve, but "seat §10 gave `process_gone`" points at a section that does not describe it.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the deliverable carries two guards but declares one negative control, which restores only part 1, leaving the review-queued window unguarded.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative control is logged "under the run directory", the same durable location §§2–6 and §15–§23 already name, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the deliverable reaches only existing symbols (`deferred_outcome`, `process_gone`, `REVIEW_QUEUED_DUTY_KIND`); no plan label, ticket number or version tag enters code, and the new test name is mechanism-named.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the review-queued window's figure ("one reflex sweep") is one the obligations deriver has no recorded source for.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — both parts serve one goal (a delivered run raises no blocking review duty before the reflex's sweep), each with its own test in the same done-when.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §33 writes `recovery_classification.py` and `obligations.py`; the section it shares a file with (§14) is already `done`, so no live writer collides and no `depends-on` edge is owed, and the open followup `f-tmstwiw-031-033` carries §33's one-line invocation.
